purpose: Single source of truth for the packages every lakehouse Spark job submits with. The Iceberg version lived in twelve files before this one existed, so raising it meant editing twelve places and nobody ever did: the deployment sat on 1.6.1 while five releases went by.

iceberg.minimum_version_reason: Before 1.8.0 the vectorized Parquet reader corrupts native memory: apache/iceberg#12178, 'Incorrect Results and SIGSEGV on Read', fixed in 1.8.0. Measured on this deployment 2026-08-29 against silver.building_register_units with vectorization on and nothing else changed: 1.6.1 died with SIGSEGV, 1.11.0 read the table. The three tables above ten million rows all died; the two in the low thousands did not, which is why it stayed hidden until a compaction run touched a large table. Root ADR-0064.
iceberg.scope: Iceberg's own storage layer. iceberg-aws-bundle backs S3FileIO, which is how Iceberg reads and writes the files of its tables. It is not the filesystem Spark reads a plain file through, which is what the hadoop block below is for.

hadoop.version_reason: Must equal the Hadoop the Spark image already carries. Measured 2026-08-31 by listing /opt/spark/jars in apache/spark:3.5.6-scala2.12-java17-python3-ubuntu: hadoop-client-api-3.3.4.jar and hadoop-client-runtime-3.3.4.jar. A different hadoop-aws brings a second copy of classes the runtime already defines.
hadoop.scope: The `s3a://` filesystem, so `spark.read` can open an object that is not part of an Iceberg table — the Silver handoff JSONL a load consumes. That image ships no aws, s3, or hadoop-cloud jar at all: 252 jars, none of them. Without this, `spark.read.json("s3a://...")` fails on the scheme while the same job writes Iceberg tables to the same bucket, because those two go through different code.

sedona.scope: Apache Sedona's spatial SQL (ST_KNN nearest-neighbour join, ST_DistanceSpheroid, the H3 functions ST_H3CellIDs and ST_H3KRing) for the Gold producers that compute what is near a parcel (root ADR-0465). Frozen with the release like the blocks above (lakehouse_engine.iceberg_packages); a session opts in with lakehouse_engine.with_sedona, which adds the extension beside Iceberg's. The Rust Silver loaders submit only the Iceberg and Hadoop blocks: they run no spatial SQL. The shaded artifact for Spark 3.5 / Scala 2.12 (the spark block), measured 2026-11-09 on Maven Central: 82,601,139 bytes, the wrapper 31,949,894.

spark.artifact_suffix_reason: The Iceberg runtime artifact name embeds both, so the artifacts above are only valid for this pair.

r2_read.reason: How every Spark and JVM read of R2 survives a reset connection, written once (root ADR-0102): drop pooled connections before R2 does (TTL, max idle), ask a broken read again after equal-jitter exponential backoff (retries, min and max wait), and let a failed task run again (local[N,task_max_failures], because plain local[N] ignores spark.task.maxFailures). lakehouse_engine reads it for the Iceberg S3FileIO catalog settings, the Hadoop s3a settings and the master URL; foundation-outbox's Rust read policy carries the same numbers and a test holds them equal. Why the task retry is the one that matters for a broken body: Iceberg's S3InputStream (1.11.0, and still on main after 1.12.0) retries only its streaming read() and only on SSL/socket-timeout/socket exceptions, and readFully(position, ...), the ranged read Parquet uses, has no retry at all; the s3.retry settings retry the SDK request up to its response headers, not the body read after it. A body cut short (2026-10-17 lineage stewardship: ConnectionClosedException, Premature end of Content-Length delimited message body, 3,208,879 of 77,287,406 bytes, in S3InputStream.readFully) therefore fails the task, and only the task's own re-run reads the range again; that job ran on a local master with no failure count, so the one failure ended it.

engines.purpose: Which engine runs what, and the ledger of what is still on Spark (root ADR-0559). DuckDB inside the Rust publisher is the engine of every transform and query; Spark's one standing role is table maintenance, started once a day. `spark_sessions` lists every file of infra/lakehouse/spark/jobs that starts a Spark session, itself or through a session builder (test_engine_ledger.SESSION_START). No file joins it. A file leaves Spark by changing its line from `wave` to `moved`: the `engine_equality` verdict it moved on (the pull request, the rows compared, and the fingerprint both engines produced). 2026-11-11: the 실거래 Gold failed 26 times at a 20 GB JVM, the rt-molit Silver load ran out of heap, Trino was killed at its container cap, and one Spark pool held 18 jobs waiting.

waves.1: Failing on JVM memory today: moved first.
waves.2: The 16 GB Gold producers and the jobs that hold the pool longest.
waves.3: The other Gold producers: the same build_or_merge seam as wave 2, so they follow its commit path.
waves.5: Geometry handoffs and served-boundary Golds that feed the tile and boundary publish.
waves.6: Table DDL, once every writer of a table is off Spark.
